_comment: The 7-piece pilot set (PRD Section 10). Title/Creator/Room/Floor come straight from the PRD's table. Creator nationality/life-dates/places and the per-artwork date_display/description/medium below are sourced from the Claude Design export's prototype copy (Gardner Lens.dc.html ARTWORK_DATA) - plausible and internally consistent with well-known public facts, but NOT confirmed as the Museum's own official curatorial text. Per user direction (2026-08-21): use it now so the app is fully populated, but treat it as unverified pending real Museum sign-off - do not present it to the Museum as final copy. accession_number stays TODO_CONTENT (never provided anywhere); seed_pilot.py refuses to treat a TODO_CONTENT value as real content. Creator date_start/date_end are free text, not numbers (per user direction 2026-08-21) - real biographical dates are often approximate/uncertain ('About 1400', '1266 or 1267'), so these must always be quoted JSON strings, e.g. "1856" not 1856. place_start/place_end may be null or omitted entirely when unknown.

artworks.title: El Jaleo
artworks.description: Sargent's monumental painting, based on drawings he made in southern Spain in 1879, is named for an Andalusian dance and is roughly translated as "the ruckus." This is a painting you can hear as well as see: heels clicking, fingers snapping, hands clapping, the sounds of singing and guitars…

artworks.title: Europa
artworks.description: Titian shows Europa carried out to sea on the back of Zeus, disguised as a bull. Painted for King Philip II of Spain, it's considered one of Titian's finest mythological paintings.

artworks.title: The Dormition and Assumption of the Virgin
artworks.description: Two scenes from the life of the Virgin Mary — her peaceful death below, her rise into heaven above — painted on a small gilded reliquary panel. It's part of a set of four scenes Fra Angelico made for the Medici family in Florence.

artworks.title: The Presentation of the Christ Child in the Temple
artworks.description: Simeon and the prophetess Anna recognize the infant Jesus as the promised savior, while the child reaches back toward his mother. It's one of seven small panels Giotto painted on the life of Christ; the others are scattered among museums in New York, London, and Munich.

artworks.title: Portrait of Isabella Stewart Gardner
artworks.description: Sargent painted Isabella Stewart Gardner in a Worth gown, standing before a red-and-gold textile. The portrait caused a stir when it was first shown — some found it too bold — and Gardner kept it largely out of public view during her lifetime.

artworks.title: Isabella Stewart Gardner in Venice
artworks.description: Isabella Stewart Gardner turns toward the viewer with her arms flung open, caught mid-motion as she returns to a room full of guests. Zorn painted the scene at the Palazzo Barbaro in Venice, capturing her legendary vivacity.

artworks.title: Self Portrait, Age 23
artworks.description: A young Rembrandt looks out from beneath a plumed cap, rendered with the loose, confident brushwork he'd become known for. It was the first painting Isabella Stewart Gardner bought with a museum collection in mind.
